result.title: Local Entropy Fluctuations for Black-Box LLM-Generated Text Detection
result.summary: Zero-shot detection of machine-generated text is vital for mitigating the risks of large language models (LLMs) misuse. While the state-of-the-art dual-model detectors and resampling-based detectors outperform single-model statistical detectors on unprompted continuations, they suffer a catastrophic breakdown on instruction-conditioned text in the black-box setting, where the source model is unknown. We analyze this failure and trace it to poor prompt conditioning for resampling-based methods and diminished cross-model discrepancy for dual-model detectors. Motivated by recent studies that human writing maintains a steady, uniform information flow, whereas machine-generated text exhibits sharp, localized entropy fluctuations, we propose a new metric, the Relative Peak Prominence Rate (RelPPR) to capture this structural contrast along the entropy trajectory and further leverage it as a signal for LLM-generated text detection. Extensive evaluations across diverse model families and datasets demonstrate that RelPPR achieves state-of-the-art black-box detection performance and remains the most reliable detector under various practical situations. Our code is available at https://github.com/brushing-git/entropy-llm-detector.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析黑盒、指令条件下重采样式与双模型检测器的失效原因，提出 Relative Peak Prominence Rate（RelPPR）指标，沿 token 熵轨迹刻画局部尖锐波动结构，用于零样本机器生成文本检测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“沿熵序列提取峰值显著性与局部波动”的轨迹统计思路，可能可供核查用于刻画 latent 推理过程中的熵/置信轨迹阶段结构与停止信号，但任务本身与视觉多模态推理无直接关联。
